assessmentSummary.identity: One Walking Quad Pull cycle is a controlled forward step, single-leg stance, ipsilateral hand hold of the ankle or foot, comfortable heel-toward-body knee-flexion and hip-extension position without forced lumbar extension, release, and step-through to the other side. It is not Walking Quad Pull with Overhead Reach, Walking Knee Hug, a stationary quad stretch, lunge, hop, balance assessment, or run.
currentCardFindings: Source 51 omits a cycle boundary, hand hold, range, support, lane, fatigue, substitution, and review contract.
Overhead reach is a changed action sequence and remains a separate card.
Two direct-title and one overhead-reach oEmbed candidates are recorded without exact-match or approval claims.
assessmentSummary.programmingDecision: Candidate-only preparation task: validate exact range, stance, lane/support, symptoms, duration, fatigue, logistics, substitutions, and downstream work; recompute after any change.

calibrationEvidence.uncertainty: No universal range, dose, recovery, readiness, outcome, or score is established; human review remains required.

currentCardSnapshot.description: In a clear level lane, take a controlled step and organize on one stance leg. Hold the ipsilateral ankle or foot lightly, bring the heel toward the body only to a comfortable knee-flexion and hip-extension position without forced lumbar extension, release, and step through before the other side. One cycle is one left and one right hold-release-step-through. This excludes overhead reach, knee hug, lunge, hop, assessment, and running.
